summary: None of the 11 spread losses were bad beats - 2 were close losses (CLE, MEM in OT) and the other 9 were real misses.
went_well: The NBA spot reads hit: fading tired or short-handed teams worked with WAS over a depleted Orlando, HOU over a back-to-back Boston, and the six-man Pacers covering; PHI, DET and LAL won going away, and CHI +3 was right as the Bears pulled away in Seattle. Heavy CBB chalk went 7-2 at -23.5 or bigger, though BKN +14.5 was a backdoor sneak-in and TTU covered by the hook, so don't count those.
went_wrong: Neutral-site ranked games went 2-3 ATS (MIA, OSU, ISU lost), and the market was right on LOU/SJU (-27.5 to -30.5) and the big dogs FDU/MILW/UTA.
improve: Before locking NBA favorites of -8 or more, confirm the final injury report and pass if a top-2 player is out or questionable.

summary: Light five-game CBB night: every favorite won (ML 5-0) but sides went 2-3, and both spread wins were backdoor covers. No bad beats - UK was a garbage-time close loss and the other two misses were real.
went_well: Not much to credit on the sides: Drexel +31.5 and Sam Houston +26.5 only got there with late garbage-time runs after trailing by 36 and 32, so those were lucky wins, not proof. The ML read was right across the board, and the Sam Houston pick did correctly bake in Alabama playing without Holloway.
went_wrong: Wofford +26.5 leaned on Tennessee's ugly exhibitions, but the Vols ran away with a 36-10 burst after half - a bad read on early-season noise. UAPB +38.5 counted on Calipari resting starters, and Arkansas won by 45 anyway; the market (and Kalshi at -40.5) had the better number. UK -32.5 was a tiny 1.5-pt edge on a huge number and the bench gave it back late.
improve: New L004: in CBB games with a 25+ point spread, only take the underdog when the model's edge is 5+ points - big dogs are 4-4 over two days with both of today's wins being backdoors, while laying 23.5+ is 7-3.

summary: No bad beats tonight: all 5 spread losses were real misses, and two wins (NOP in OT, LAL covering by 1.5) were tight.
went_well: Taking points against big favorites hit: MIL +11.5 (L001 passed on BOS with Tatum resting, and the Bucks rallied from 22 down), DAL +11.5 and MIN +8.5, who won outright. The road-dominance read on POR -3.5 (won by 13) and fading tired Toronto with DEN -4.5 (won by 19) were right too; NOP -5.5 only got there in OT, so don't count that one.
went_wrong: MEM -6.5 lost outright to a short-handed Pacers team, ATL beat WAS by 15 even without Jalen Johnson, CHI +12.5 got buried by an 84-point Knicks first half, and OKC (SGA 42) was just better than CLE +2.5 - the line was right there.
improve: New L005: when an NBA favorite of -5+ is priced up mostly because the other team is banged up, only lay it with a 2+ pt model edge - MEM -6.5 on a 1.5-pt edge lost outright to depleted Indiana. Also treat a line move against the public as a tiebreaker, not a reason on its own: DET -2.5 leaned on that and lost by 6.

summary: Split night on the sides at 6-5 ATS but the favorites nearly ran the table on the ML (10-1). No bad beats: Florida was a close garbage-time miss by 2.5 and the other 4 losses were real misses.
went_well: The Miami fade was the read of the night: tired Heat on the second night of a back-to-back, line moving against 83% of the public, and the Warriors ran away in the second half by 20. L004 also went 3-0 by steering us onto Duke, Michigan State and Illinois instead of the dogs, and all three covered with room to spare; Vandy and Texas were clean covers too.
went_wrong: Both small-edge plays on short-handed teams were bad reads: Ravens +10.5 with a rookie QB lost by 23 after three turnovers, and Orlando without Banchero and Suggs coughed it up 25 times and lost by 13 to a Suns team on a back-to-back. Texas Tech and Arizona were 'line was right' misses where the dogs kept scoring, so laying 25+ went 4-3 tonight.
improve: New L006: when backing a team missing its starting QB or two-plus starters, require a 2+ point edge or side with the healthy team - it's the mirror of L005, which keeps us from overrating those injuries the other way. Keep using L004 on 25+ CBB spreads (3-0 so far), but don't change how we handle laying big CBB numbers off one 4-3 night - TTU and ARIZ were the market being right, not a pattern yet.

summary: No bad beats: NOP (blew a 4th-quarter lead) and Michigan (lost +7.5 by the hook) were close losses, the other 11 were real misses. TCU-Arizona went final later (ARIZ 29-28), so TCU +7.5 and the ARIZ ML both won.
went_well: Mavs -7.5 was right that Utah is bad beyond its injuries (L005 check passed), and L006 steering us to Lakers -2.5 over a short-handed Portland paid off behind Luka's 53. Illinois +4.5 read Nebraska's slide correctly and won outright, and KU, BYU and UCLA all blew out their big numbers; ATL by the hook and SAC inside 17.5 were too close to count as proof.
went_wrong: The POTD was a bad read: we figured a banged-up OKC was beatable, and Ajay Mitchell's 35 ran Memphis off the floor. Philly -2.5 (line flipped with the public) lost by 24, and the money-split dogs MIL, VT and Nevada all got buried. Big CBB chalk went 3-5 at 25+, with UK, Bama, Iowa State, Miami and UVA all falling short; the market was right there.
improve: New L007: line moves and money splits are a tiebreaker, not a reason - when they're the main case for a pick, require a 2.5+ pt model edge or pass (those picks went 1-5 tonight after DET lost the same way Nov 4). L004 is now 5-4; keep testing it, but note UK and ISU were forced onto chalk the model leaned against and both missed.

summary: No bad beats: TAMU, KU, MSST, Rutgers and BC (by the hook) were close losses, the rest were real misses.
went_well: Laying points with teams we actually liked was the story: Texas, Utah, UCLA, Tennessee, Duke, Louisville and Boise all covered comfortably, and L004 (Zags -27.5) and L006 (Spurs -5.5) both cashed big. Nebraska -2.5 at a neutral site and Clemson -2.5 (L007) were clean small-edge wins; GSW only covered thanks to OT and MIA only by the hook, so those don't count as proof.
went_wrong: The POTD was a bad read: Houston fell behind 35-23 early and Booker closed it, so -7.5 on the road was too much faith in the Rockets. Ohio State and Purdue lost outright as favorites, and the split plays (favorite ML, dog spread) went 7-10, with Ole Miss, Kansas State and Merrimack getting buried; the dogs that won outright (Bama, OU, MSU, Georgetown) also cost us on the ML side.
improve: New L008: when we like the favorite to win, stop grabbing the dog's points; lay the favorite's number or pass (split picks are 21-27 ATS so far). Keep L001 testing; WAS +11.5 lost by 39 even with OKC short-handed, so getting points against a depleted favorite isn't automatically value.

summary: No bad beats: Dallas (by the hook), the Saints in OT and Houston-Cal (1.5 short) were close losses, the other 8 were real misses.
went_well: Laying it with teams we liked worked again: KC, Houston and Boston blew out their numbers and L008 went 5-2 on its first day (LA, KC, DET, HOU, BOS covered). Dallas -9.5 fading the Nets on a back-to-back, Giants -2.5 over Philly's third-string QB and St. John's -28.5 (L004) were clean reads, and TB +6.5 and SAC +8.5 were right on the number.
went_wrong: The NBA spot fades were bad reads: Pistons -4.5 counted on a tired Lakers team and Reaves dropped 43 without Luka, and Pelicans -1.5 lost by 16 to a Clippers team we wrote off for its injuries. NE -3.5 was a bad read with Maye throwing 3 picks, SF's defense buried LV +9.5, and the market was right on SEA over ARI, MIN without Edwards and PHI -9.5 in Chicago.
improve: New L009: in the NBA, when the main case is the other team's injuries or a tired/travel spot, require a 2.5+ pt model edge at any spread (L005 only covers -5+ favorites) and keep those plays out of the POTD - DET and NOP were 1-2 pt edges. Keep L008 going (5-2 so far); no change off DAL, NO or Houston-Cal, which were close losses.

record: Spread 86-65 (57.0% vs 52.4% breakeven) · ML 124-27 · POTD 2-5 · 0 bad beats in 65 spread losses
summary: None of the 65 spread losses were bad beats; 12 were close losses (3 by the hook), 24 were bad reads and 21 were the line being right.
went_well: Every league was over breakeven ATS (NFL 9-6, NBA 31-23, CBB 28-21, CFB 18-15), and favorites carried it at 57-32 (CBB 22-13, NBA 18-10, CFB 10-6, NFL 7-3). Reads that faded teams on a back-to-back went 11-3, L004 is 7-4 by steering big CBB spreads onto chalk, L006 is 2-0 and L008 started 5-2.
went_wrong: Underdogs went 29-33 ATS and split picks (favorite ML, dog spread) went 23-31, which is why L008 exists.
improve: Apply L008 (lay the favorite or pass on split picks) and new L009 (2.5+ pt edge for NBA injury/spot fades, never the POTD) every day, and pick the POTD from the strongest healthy-favorite read. No lesson reached 15 picks, so nothing was kept or dropped this week; all nine stay Testing, with L004 (7-4) closest to Keep and L001 (1-2) the one to watch.

summary: A break-even day on the sides at 8-8 ATS and 12-4 straight up, with a slightly positive +0.2 CLV. Of the 8 spread losses, Cincinnati was a bad beat and Indiana (late backdoor) and Denver (1.5 short) were close losses; the other 5 were real misses.
went_well: Healthy-favorite reads delivered: Spurs -8.5 (POTD) won by 26 behind Wemby's 40, Bills -3 smothered Wentz (L006/L008), and flipping to Warriors -8.5 once Zion and Murphy sat was right. Big CBB chalk went 3-2 with Miami, UConn (L004) and Bama all winning by 38+; Dallas and Detroit only covered by the hook, so those don't prove much.
went_wrong: Hawks +2.5 fading a back-to-back Lakers team was a bad read on a 3-pt edge, and Cavs -8.5 lost outright to a gutted Charlotte team on a 1.5-pt edge, exactly the spot L005 warns about. The market was right on Toronto (DK even dropped to -2.5) and on Tennessee and Texas falling short of 28.5 and 35.5.
improve: Actually apply L005 to NBA favorites of -5+ priced up for the opponent's injuries (CLE -8.5 on a 1.5 edge should have been a pass) and L010/L009 to 3+ pt edges on tired-team fades like ATL +2.5. No new lesson from Cincinnati, Indiana or Denver, which were a bad beat and close losses.

summary: Rough night on the spread at 6-11, though 11-6 straight up with a slightly positive +0.2 CLV. Of the 11 spread losses, Miami (Utah's 37-point 4th) was a bad beat and Florida (hook) and Iowa (OT) were close losses; the other 8 were real misses.
went_well: Healthy favorites came through again: Knicks -15.5 rolled a Giannis-less Milwaukee by 32, Kansas -4.5 beat Kentucky by 20, and sticking with the back-to-back Suns over a short-handed Clippers team (L009) won by 23. Iowa State -33.5 covered at the better FanDuel number (+2 CLV).
went_wrong: The CBB lesson flips hurt: the model leaned Florida State, Virginia Tech, Michigan State and K-State, and L008/L011 moved all four to the favorite; only Florida came close. Philly +1.5 ignored a line that flipped against the public money and lost by 22, OKC -1.5 got run off the floor in Portland, and the big CBB chalk (BYU, Arizona, UVA POTD) all fell short as benches played the second half.
improve: Watch L008 (now 7-7) and L011 (1-4): if CBB flips of a 1-1.5 pt dog lean keep losing this week, they should be narrowed to the NBA. New L012: when the line moves against our side despite the money being on it, pass or switch unless the edge is 2.5+.

summary: Close to even on the spread at 8-9 and a strong 15-2 straight up, with a +0.4 CLV, so the numbers we got were mostly good. Of the 9 spread losses, LAL (Bucks' 39-pt 4th) was a bad beat and NEB (hook) and MEM (by 1.5) were close losses; the other 6 were real misses.
went_well: The big CBB chalk mostly came through under L004/L010: St. John's -27.5 (+1 CLV), Houston -36.5 and UCLA -44.5 rolled, and USC -8.5 at Cal pulled away. Portland +1.5 read the OKC rematch right, Michigan -3.5 beat Marquette by 14, and TOR +7.5 against a back-to-back Boston covered at a number 2 points better than the close.
went_wrong: Bad reads in the NBA: the Knicks lost outright to Cleveland, the Pelicans got run by a 3-8 Nets team after Murphy and Mathurin fell out, Utah collapsed vs Orlando, and Chicago nearly beat the Spurs outright on a -14.5. Indiana's 13-point win over Washington was a line-was-right loss after L012 flipped us to the dog, and Arkansas -31.5 fell well short.
improve: NBA dogs picked while we still had the favorite to win (TOR, WAS, MEM, UTA) went 1-3; when L005/L006/L012 point to that kind of split, L008 (now Keep) should win and we lay the favorite or pass.

summary: Tough spread night at 2-5 on a small 7-game board, but 6-1 straight up and +0.4 CLV, so we mostly got good numbers. No bad beats: Toronto (hook), Phoenix (1.5 short) and the Giants (late Diggs TD) were close losses, and Detroit and BYU were real misses.
went_well: Minnesota -5.5 crushed Dallas by 39 and Texas A&M -7.5 (L008 flip, +1 CLV) pulled away by 19 even without Cade Phillips. Toronto +10.5 beat the close by 3 points after PHI's late injury news, a good number even though it lost by the hook.
went_wrong: Detroit -9.5 (POTD) underrated a Washington team with Trae Young and Anthony Davis, who dragged it to double OT. BYU -23.5 was a bad flip: L010/L011 talked us off a big Montana State lean, BYU won by 15 and the raw number was closer.
improve: New L016: in CBB, stop letting L011 flip a dog lean onto the favorite (CBB flips are 1-5, NBA 2-0); keep the dog or pass. That's three straight POTD losses, so before locking a road favorite POTD, check that the home side isn't getting healthy stars back (one game, not a new lesson yet).
